notes.title: 0.4.2.1 hotfix
notes.content: +hopefully fixed meta unlock ui sometimes disappearing

As I said in the patch notes for 0.4.1, I wanted to focus on filling out other areas of the game RuneLight is lacking in. so without further ado...
[h1]Meta Progress[/h1]
Before, RuneLight was completely lacking in any meta progress. This update, I have added [b]18 new meta unlocks[/b] in the form of starter equipment, which can be chosen before entering a run. While they're not the most powerful of equipment, each item has a build they can be slotted into, or work as stepping stones to force certain builds earlier. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44116119/964ecd348b1843507c313d0a00f8c3b2c3c9059f.png[/img]
[h2]Achievements[/h2]
I have also added [b]new achievements[/b] to go along with each of the meta unlocks, plus a bonus achievement for beating the game with no equipment
[h1]New Player Experience[/h1]
For 0.4.2, I wanted to take some steps to smoothen out the new player experience so the game is more approachable.
[h2]Tutorial[/h2]
I added a [b]new tutorial to explain the basics of the game[/b]. it's just a few quick popup boxes that explain each main component of the game. I'll be gathering feedback and seeing how people interact with the tutorial and making adjustments as I see fit
[h2]Level up changes[/h2]
I personally witnessed people roll over key items without knowing it, and the rate at which players gained new weapons was inconsistent. To remedy this, I [b]added a guaranteed weapon equipment on level 8[/b], which cannot be skipped.
[h2]Difficulty Settings[/h2]
One big thing RuneLight was lacking is a proper difficulty curve. To remedy this, I added [b]two new difficulties, one easier and one harder[/b]. Players can now choose a difficulty more in line with the game they want to play, whether that's sit back and relax or lock in to survive.

Right now, the difficulty system is exclusively stat modifications, which isn't really interesting or fun. In the future, [b]when I rework the maps, I will be overhauling the difficulty system to be more of an ascension climb[/b], but for the time being this will have to do.

[h1]Balance[/h1]
[b]0.4.2 Majorly shifts the damage and balance meta [/b]
I wanted to give each of the status effects more impact, make them better to use. but the issue was statuses and crowd control didn't matter because most things die in one or two hits. so I nerfed everything.
[list]
[*] [Buff]ALL weapons now have more consistent damage range, from -5 - +5 to -2 - +2
[/list]
Starting Weapons have all had their damage majorly cut
[list]
[*] [Nerf]Base projectile 20 damage -> 10 damage
[*] [Buff]all Projectiles now have 20% damage falloff, previously 50%
[*] [Nerf]Base Grenade 20 damage -> 10 Damage
[*] [Nerf]Base Orbiter 10 damage -> 8 Damage
[*] [Nerf]Base Blast 18 damage -> 9 Damage
[*] [Nerf]Base Pulse 30 Damage -> 14 Damage
[/list]
The equipment weapons and their upgrades have had their base damage cut in half, following the scaling nerf from 0.4.1
[list]
[*] [Nerf]Spiked shoes 5 damage -> 3 damage
[*] [Nerf]Magic Shield 25 damage -> 12 damage
[*] [Nerf]Philosopher's Orb 10 Damage -> 7 Damage
[*] [Nerf]Sorcerer's Robes 10 Damage -> 5
[*] [Nerf]Sorcerer's Robes now have a 0.25s Cooldown
[*] [Nerf]Root Boots 20 Damage -> 10 Damage
[*] [Nerf]Ripostal Wraps 25 Damage -> 12
[*] [Nerf]Spike Charm 15 Damage -> 7 Damage
[*] [Nerf]Dark Helmet 15 Damage -> 7 Damage
[*] [Nerf]Hunting Tracker 20 Damage -> 10 Damage
[*] [Nerf]Bloody Coat 30 Damage -> 15 Damage
[/list]
The Set Bonus Weapons had their scaling cut majorly. Some of the weaker ones got buffed to compensate
[list]
[*] [Nerf]Energy Javelins 2 Damage per Speed -> 1 Damage per Speed
[*] [Nerf]Sunsteel Shield 0.5 Damage per Armor -> 0.25 Damage per Armor
[*] [Buff]Sunsteel Shield 0.2s Cooldown -> 0.15s Cooldown
[*] [Nerf]Scholar's Stance 2.25 Damage per Wisdom -> 1.5 Damage per Wisdom
[*] [Nerf]Duelist's Strike 1.5 Damage per Dodge -> 1 Damage per Dodge
[*] [Buff]Inertia Bolt has more range
[*] [Nerf]Timed Detonators 1.5 Damage per item Droprate -> 1 Damage per item Droprate
[*] [Nerf]Explosive Leap 2 Damage per Dash Speed -> 1 Damage per Dash Speed
[*] [Nerf]Crystal Heart 1 Damage per Regeneration Point -> 0.75 Damage per Regeneration, 5 Base -> 2 Base
[*] [Nerf]Cursed Body 1.5 Damage per Spawnrate Point -> 0.5 Damager per Spawnrate Point
[/list]

While the damage potential for every weapon has gone down, to compensate [b]I have doubled the effect of every debuff[/b]. Additionally, I have increased the effects of the non-elemental debuffs to match their elemental counterparts. The inital idea was they were weaker because they could be stacked infinitely, but in practice, they would rarely match their elemental counterparts before the enemy died.
[list]
[*] [Buff] Shocked is now +10% damage per stack
[*] [Buff] Fear is now +10% damage per stack
[*] [Buff] Turtle Gloves +3% damage per bleed -> +5% damage per bleed
[*] [Buff] Fire 3 Damage per Tick -> 6 Damage per Tick
[*] [Buff] Bleed 2 Damage per Tick -> 6 Damage per Tick
[*] [Buff] Iced -10% attack speed -> -20% attack speed
[*] [Buff] Rooted -10% movement -> -20% movement
[*] [Buff] Fatigued -10% movement -> -20% movement
[/list]
Additionally, Nature charm's movement slowing was much more impactful than Frost charm's attack speed slowing, so I flipped their damage penalties
[list]
[*] [Nerf] Nature charm -15% damage -> -45% damage
[*] [Buff] Frost charm -45% damage -> -15% damage
[/list]

Because cutting the base damage of everything also nerfed the damage charms as a side effect, I buffed them to compensate.
[list]
[*] [Buff]Power Charm +35% Damage -> +50% Damage
[*] [Buff]Sharpness Charm +70% Crit Mult -> +100% Crit Mult
[/list]
The dynamic crit charms were also numerically worse than the flat crit chance charm, so I buffed them
[list]
[*] [Buff]Momentum Charm +1% per dash point -> +3% per 2 dash points
[*] [Buff]Riposte Charm +1% per 3 dodge -> +3% per 2 dodge
[*] 
[/list]

[h2]misc changes[/h2]
equipment
[list]
[*] resprited and renamed runner's gloves and super speed gloves
[*] reworked knight's boots and upgrades
[*] renamed knight's boots and first upgrade path
[*] [buff] lightning charge bands +50% Dash Recharge -> +60%
[*] [buff] elven steel boots +6% Dash Recharge per Speed Boost -> +8%
[/list]

maps
[list]
[*] slightly reduced spawnrate of the crystal golems on the forest
[/list]
visuals
[list]
[*] exp bar now shows level rather than exp required
[*] completely redid end of run screen
[*] Charms with scalar effects now show how much stats they give
[/list]
misc
[list]
[*] added two additional resolutions, 1600x900 and 2560x1440
[/list]
bug fixes
[list]
[*] fighting spirit description now correctly say epic
[*] fighting spirit description no longer has regeneration popup attached
[*] healing hands description now correctly say legendary
[*] in game settings now correctly display credits on page 3
[/list]
[h2]What's next[/h2]
The next update is going to be a major update, version 0.5. This will be a milestone update that brings a lot of content and mechanical updates, and as such it will be a while before it's ready. The focus of the update will be adding more weapons and weapon modifiers. I don't want to promise anything before it's set in stone, but I expect the update to be out in Q4 of 2024. I will be sharing more along the way
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44116119/ea6b322abd38a783bc75ecc8d8e1a25396d3acc9.png[/img]

notes.title: 0.4.1 OUT NOW
notes.content:
[h1]What's new[/h1]
[h2]Mechanics[/h2]
For 0.4.1, I [b]reworked my approach to item pickups[/b] and the equipment centered around it. Because every effect modification was applied to the same pickup, in order to use one effect optimally you would have to use every other effect suboptimally.
Instead, many [b]equipment pieces add a new potential item drop[/b] to the enemies, each with it's own effect.
-completely reworked and renamed magic gloves and upgrades. now an accessory named 'spike charm'
-reworked functionality of runner's gloves[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44116119/db7824d8e73e1803d3e40f17bb07755175e17a37.png[/img] and upgrades.
-reworked Collector's Intuition[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44116119/ee735dc873aab2d7527e4d7ef9d6010f5ce44aec.png[/img] to optimally use the new pickups
-reworked Constructor's Cloak[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44116119/06182badf9b6346d58251ee82ae3751b7e730f44.png[/img]. I wonder what it does..
[h2]equipment[/h2]
Added [b]8 brand new equipment pieces[/b], increasing the [b]overall pool by 20%.[/b] There was no archetype of focus this time. instead, each archetype should now feel more fleshed out
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44116119/80e33b0ab7e36574bc29d69ebb05784d77180dd1.png[/img]
[h1]What's Changed[/h1]
[h2]Weapons[/h2]
The [b]Projectile[/b] Weapon was meant to be a long range projectile based attack, much like the grenade is a long ranged area attack. However, it's high damage and straight-forward targeting made it much better than the other weapons, so I [b]nerfed it's damage down from 25 to 20[/b]

[h2]Equipment[/h2]
[b]Lowered the scaling on most equipment weapons from 20% to 10%[/b]. These items were previously capable of reaching really high numbers with minimal effort, so I had to scale them back a little

[h2]map changes[/h2]
-Made minute 10 great again

[h2]Visual Changes[/h2]
-moved enemy healthbars to below
-added new indicators for the various enemy debuffs

[h2]bug fixes[/h2]
-Elven Steel Braces now have correct player sprite.
-fixed description of hunting tracker and upgrades
-fixed description of demon helmet
-fixed description of sorcerer's robes and upgrades
-fixed shot angles of sorcerer's robes and upgrades
-fixed info box for Ironskin

[h1]What's next[/h1]
Now that RuneLight has a significantly increased item pool and the archetypes are more fleshed out, it's time to focus my attention on other areas the game is lacking in. [b]Next update will introduce the first batch of meta unlocks[/b], as well as steam  achievements. I don't want to promise exact dates, but expect 0.4.2 to [b]release Q1 2025[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44116119/379c40fa062cc555496e513b3c5ca7fb7bb292b3.png[/img]

notes.title: RuneLight 0.4
notes.content:
[h1]The modification update[/h1]
Weapon modifiers have been expanded. now EVERY weapon in the game can have stat modifiers attached, allowing you to greatly change your build's final results and power. This, however, required some major reworks to the weapon charms to compensate
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44116119/215fb6c35184d03195c80d9495ef872da70c65ee.gif[/img]
[h1]Weapons[/h1]
Your primary attack can now only have up to 4 modifiers (-2)
[h2]Weapon Charms[/h2]
[b]Weapon Charms can no longer be upgraded[/b]. I chose to go this route for three reasons:
[b]Attainability[/b]: it was nearly impossible to achieve a 'complete' weapon build and keep up with equipment. players felt encouraged to super buff a single weapon rather than increase the power of all of their weapons, which wasn't the intent.
[b]Balance[/b]: upgraded basic charms almost always outperformed the un-upgraded scalar charms, and getting 3 of the same scalar charm was too unreliable.
[b]Future proofing[/b]: my plans for the future of RuneLight include more than doubling the amount of weapon charms available, which would just make the first two problems even more pronounced
I have buffed most of the base charms to compensate.

[list]
[*] [Buff] Power Charm +15% damage (20->35)
[*] [Buff] Pierce Charm +1 Pierce (+2->+3)
[*] [Buff] Projectile Charm +20% damage (-20 -> 0)
[*] [Buff] Size Charm +10% Size (+10 -> +20)
[*] [Buff] Charge Charm +15% Attack Speed (+15 -> +30)
[*] [Buff] Precision Charm +12% Crit Chance (+8 -> +20)
[*] [Buff] Sharpness Charm +30% Crit Mult (+40 -> +70)
[/list]

[h2]Elements[/h2]
[b]All element charms have been completely reworked[/b]. Elements can now be applied to every weapon, and each element now has an associated debuff. Elements can no longer be upgraded, and each element now subtracts [i]percent [/i]damage rather than [i]base [/i]damage
[list]
[*] [b]Fire[/b] now does 3 damage per stack per tick. 3 ticks per second
[*] [b]Storm [/b]now causes enemies to take 5% more damage per stack from all sources
[*] [b]Ice [/b]now causes enemies to attack slower
[*] [b]Nature [/b]now causes enemies to move slower
[/list]
I know this takes away some of the "rule of cool" of the previous element system, for example the wind orbiters knocking back enemies. This is something I will be looking to rectify in the future
 
[h1]Other new mechanics[/h1]
[list]
[*] you can now reroll level up rewards once per level up
[*] you can now skip rewards to get 25% of the exp refunded
[/list]
These changes were made to make getting the things you want more reliable, especially as I intend to add many, many more equipment and weapon mods to the game in the future.

[h1]Other Changes[/h1]
[h2]Visuals[/h2]
[list]
[*] reworked most weapon visuals
[*] added entity shadows
[*] updated terrain art and visuals for the forest and beach maps
[*] resprited some enemies on the forest and beach maps
[/list]
[h2]balance[/h2]
[h3]Set Bonuses[/h3]
[list]
[*] Dodge Set Attack Size is now 0.6T radius [-0.4]
[/list]
[h3]map changes[/h3]
[list]
[*] reduced elite spawnrate for forest and beach 
[*] overhauled spawns on forest and beach
[/list]
[b]Forest[/b]
[list]
[*] burrower and evolved burrower now deal less damage
[*] walking mountain now deals less damage
[*] walking mountain now has a lot more health
[/list]
[h2]UI and UX changes[/h2]
[list]
[*] completely redid level selection ui
[*] overhauled set bonus display ui
[*] updated end of run screen to fit the new weapons
[*] redid main menu screen
[*] completely redid options ui. should be easier to nagivate
[*] added a lot more gameplay options
	-auto fill empty equipment
[*] added more visual settings
 	-borderless window
 	-pause while tabbed out
[*] made the ingame ui more uniform
[/list]
[h2]bug fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] made a lot of performance optimizations. game should no longer struggle with high spawnrate builds
[*] fixed some crashes related to enemies on the beach map
[*] enemies should no longer push each other around when the game is paused
[/list]
[h1]What's next[/h1]
I'd like to be more transparent on what comes next, especially since I recently increased the price of RuneLight to go along with this update.
The next update will be 0.4.1, and is slotted to release early next month. The update will primarily be focused on adding new equipment, fleshing out the item pools that are currently lacking.
I've also created a visual roadmap to mark the game's overall progress on content
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44116119/6458d44afa9696249b76b8ef90915a5b4a3a2ab1.png[/img]

notes.title: Upcoming Price Update
notes.content:
Hello, Elmok here. While the next update for RuneLight isn't [i]quite[/i] ready yet, I have an important announcement on the future. In (just under) 2 weeks, [b]on October 18,2024, RuneLight will be going from 5 USD to 10 USD[/b]. This is to go along with [b]major update 0.4, which will release the following week[/b] on October 25, 2024

[h2]Why?[/h2]
When I first priced RuneLight, I was planning a much smaller scoped and simple game. However, that original vision wasn't shaping up to be a fun game, so a little over a year ago I decided to majorly rescope, expand on, and rework RuneLight. I have put a lot more work into making the game better, and I believe it is fair to increase the price to reflect the larger scope and effort going into it

[h2]Why now?[/h2]
The price is increasing to go along with the 0.4 update, which is an important benchmark. As of 0.4, I consider RuneLight to be [b]feature complete [/b] in regards to the core mechanics. Other than a few smaller features like proper boss fights and additional primary weapons, the gameplay of 0.4 is the same gameplay you can expect from the full release

[h2]Will RuneLight increase in price again?[/h2]
No. At some point you have to decide where to draw the line in the sand and define what will and will not make it into the game, and over the past couple weeks I've been really ironing out what will and will not make it into 1.0 and what price I believe to be fair for the content RuneLight offers.

As such, [b]any future expansions to the game's scope will come as either free post 1.0 updates or potentially paid dlc, but the base game of RuneLight will always be 10USD[/b]

[h2]What happens next?[/h2]
within the next week I will be releasing a detailed roadmap and video laying out exactly what my plans are so you can know exactly what to expect going forwards. A week later, the price will go up from 5USD to 10USD, as well as teasers for 0.4, an update to the trailer and promotional material. The following week 0.4 will come out

notes.title: RuneLight 0.3
notes.content:
[h1]new mechanics[/h1]
I expanded on the set bonuses added in the last update by adding 9 brand new attacks, unlocked by getting 5 of their respectively tagged items. This allows more support oriented builds and equipment to keep pace with the enemy waves
[h2]equipment[/h2]
Instead of adding new equipment, I decided to focus on revamping the first batch of equipment added in 0.3.
[Balance, Buff] Magnet Gloves Upgrade 2 now deals +2 Damage (10->12)
[Balance, Nerf] Tome of Knowledge Upgrade 1 now spawns less experience (3/second -> 2/second)
[Balance, Buff] Tome of Knowledge Upgrade 1 now deals a small blast on spawned experience
[Balance, Rework] Collecter's Cloak and Upgrades no longer have a cap on stored pickups
[Balance, Buff] Collecter's Cloak Upgrade 1 auto-uses pickups at low health
[Balance, Buff] Collecter's Cloak Upgrade 2 is now permanent +5 Item Droprate
[Balance, Rework]Cross Cloak Upgrade 2 no longer gives speed and dodge, now gives 3 regen. now has Healer Tag.
[Balance, Rework]Energy Bracers Upgrade 2 now creates spikes on Dash
[Balance, Nerf]Ninja Boots and Upgrades now capped at +10
[Balance, Reworf]Ninja Boots Path 1 now releases projectiles on reset
[Balance, Nerf]Crimson Scythe -20% Chance (50% -> 30%)
[Balance, Nerf]Crimson Scythe Path 1 -20% Chance (100% -> 80%)
[Balance, Nerf]Crimson Scythe Path 2 -30% Chance (50% -> 30%)
[Balance, Rework]Crimson Scythe Path 2 now attacks nearby enemies
[Balance, Rework]Brawlers' Breastplate now accessory, renamed to Cursed Amulet. Reworked Upgrades
[Balance, Nerf]Healing Hands now legendary
[Balance, Buff]Fighting Spirit now epic

[b]UI changes[/b]
Added a new end of run summary screen when winning or dying

[b]bug fixes[/b]
game should no longer softlock when dying or winning under certain circumstances

[b]What's Next[/b]
Next update I'm planning is going to be big. It's too soon to promise anything, but the next update will change the game in fundamental ways. Unfortunately, it's going to be a while before it comes out. this is for three major reasons
[olist]
[*] Like I just mentioned, I have big plans for the next update. Expect no part of the game to go untouched.
[*] I'm also back in school. This means the time I have to work on RuneLight is dramatically reduced
[*] I want to explore other game ideas. I feel I've been putting all my eggs in one basket by working on Runelight for almost a year and a half exclusively, and I want to spread my wings a little. will post more on that later
[/olist]

notes.title: RuneLight 0.3.2
notes.content:
It took longer than I had hoped, but it's finally here, 0.3.2!
[h1]new mechanics[/h1]
Added Set Bonuses. the tags I introduced in the last update have been turned into set bonuses, granting up to 10 of their respective stats. the goal is to reduce reliance on equipment charms to get builds off the ground.
[h2]General and Important Balance[/h2]
The equipment charms have had some of their stats shifted into the set bonuses. Overall stats should end up higher for completed builds
[list]
[*] All base charms now give 2 of their stat (-1)
[*] All path 1 charms now give 5 of their stat (-2)
[*] All path 2 charms now give 3 of their primary stat (-2)
[/list]
Some of the player stats needed to be nerfed due to the overall higher stats
[list]
[*] Base Regeneration is now 50% less. This affects all increases to Regeneration
[*] Base Dash Distance is now 14% Shorter. This affects all increases to dash distance
[/list]
Additionally, enemy and player scaling was in need of some adjustment
[list]
[*] Enemy Count Scaling Adjusted
[*] All enemies now deal at least 1 contact damage. this allows every enemy to trigger certain effects
[*] Item Rarity Chances Adjusted
[/list]
I also wanted Ironskin to be more in line with the other player buffs
[list]
[*] Ironskin is now +1 armor per stack, no longer has speed penalty
[/list]
[h2]equipment[/h2]
[list]
[*] [new]A Healing and Pickup item
[*] [new]A Healing and Dash item
[*] [new]A Healing and Standing Still item
[*] [new]A Healing and Taking Damage item
[*] [new]A Healing and Experience item
[*] [new]A Healing and Enemy Spawn item
[*] [new]A dodge and Enemy Spawn item
[*] [new]A dodge and Healing item
[*] [rework]Reworked Topaz Tunic and upgrades
[*] [rework]Reworked Chalice of Blood and upgrades
[*] [nerf]Tome of Elven Curses is now legendary
[*] [nerf]Winged Boots is now Epic
[*] [buff]Magic Stopwatch is now Epic
[*] [buff]Intagibilit-Orb is now Rare
[*] [nerf]Root Boots no longer gives armor while standing still, in regards to the set bonuses
[*] [nerf]Emerald Entity now deals 20 damage (-10)
[/list]

notes.title: RuneLight 0.3
notes.content:
[h1]The Archetypes[/h1]
The Archetypes are the main focus and goal of 0.3, aiming to add a lot more run variety and build diversity. There are currently 10 Archetypes in the game to build around, each with their own scalar stats and equipment. Some of the equipment features simple but unique stat increases, like 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44116119/37edee2706cef097563f55ce96e38244e4e14ef2.png[/img]
other equipment is more involved, adding new behaviors and mechanics. for example,
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44116119/cab4fd5965b145dfa07f417baeef22686cde6146.png[/img]
Finally, some equipment seeks to bring your strength to new heights by adding additional attacks. For example, 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44116119/eefa9c851f9a647d8437ba4e73cd2785291d7e92.png[/img]

[h2]Other Changes[/h2]
I've spent the last several months overhauling pretty much every aspect of the game. Weapon modifiers have been expanded, Player stats and abilities have been increased, many of the enemies have been updated, and there's a new map to experiment with.

[b]Weapon Changes[/b]
[list]
[*] Weapon Modifiers have been rebalanced and for the most part nerfed
[*] Mana, Mana cost, and Cooldown have been reworked and rolled into one stat
[*] Added over a dozen new weapon modifiers. some are simple, like
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44116119/1a0e31532cde9371c3532fd479b2de5c540b67ac.png[/img]
other weapon modifiers are a bit more involved and scale dynamically, like
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44116119/fca2a8b5e93025f7d8dc83ece393ab0d09a83055.png[/img]
These dynamically scaling charms seek to bridge the gap between your player's stats and build and your weapon's stats
[/list]
[b]Player Stats and Abilities[/b]
[list]
[*] Removed Mana and Mana Regen
[*] Added the ability to Dash
[*] Added 3 new stats, for a total of 9
[*] Added new charms to reflect these stats
[/list]
[b]Map and Enemies[/b]
[list]
[*] Enemies can now drop item pickups, which heal up to 10 health on use
[*] reworked many of the enemies on the Forest map
[*] Added a new map, the Beach
[/list]
[b]Other changes[/b]
In addition to new content and mechanics, I've also drastically reworked the game's art and presentation
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44116119/1f451b1eaca11e214298b30636c2994c4d8310de.png[/img]

[h3]What Comes next[/h3]
After 0.3, I believe RuneLight is finally in a good state mechanically. As such, instead of spending multiple months working on one major update, I've decided to split 0.4 into a series of 10 smaller updates. These updates will include lots more equipment, reworks to existing equipment, mechanics to balance out the larger pool (like rarity and weights), improved menus and ui, and a map to finish things off. I'll try to have updates out every 2-4 weeks, and I'll post announcements for any delays. Looking immediately forward, I expect to have a mini patch addressing smaller feedback out this weekend.

notes.title: RuneLight 0.2
notes.content:
[h1]New Content[/h1]
[b]Weapons Rework[/b]
[list]
[*] weapon system split into 2 parts, the weapons and the elements
[*] 4 base weapons to choose from

[/list]

[/list]

[list]

[/list]

[list]

[/list]
[h3]What Comes Next[/h3]
This update took way longer to complete than I thought it would, and I definitely went silent for the last couple months there. I would like to remedy this by releasing monthly progress updates detailing what I've been working on. I've already began planning the next major update, and am excited to share what comes next. things to expect:
[list]
[*] Reintroduction of the Island map, with new enemies and visuals to match the Forest Map
[*] Adding a higher emphasis on builds and run variety
[*] over 50+ new modifiers 
[/list]

notes.title: RuneLight Update Roadmap
notes.content:
Hello everybody! Elmok here. Things have been a bit quiet, but I'm hard at work on the first major update for RuneLight. Unfortunately this update will probably take multiple weeks if not months to fully deliver on, so I created this visual roadmap to track my progress in the meantime!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44116119/55f8db0857ed60e1ac970b5756f10284e885ad00.png[/img]

Let's break down exactly what the roadmap means:

[b]Weapons:[/b]obviously, I have deemed this update the weapons update. I believe Runelight does not have enough weapons and weapon variations to keep the game interesting for extended periods of time, and I'd like to spend the first major update correcting this issue. I plan to go from the game's current 8 weapons to 24. Each of the small squares represents 1 weapon with 2 evolutions.

[b]Resprites:[/b]I'm not happy with most of RuneLight's current art and visuals. I wouldn't go as far as to say it's [i]bad[/i], but I will say it is boring, basic, uninspired. Over the next few updates I plan to rework pretty much every aspect of the game's visuals, starting with the player. I have provided a sketch of the player's design as well as marked the animations the player will need. 

[b]Enemies:[/b] I'm not happy with the current map system. I think it's basic and boring, and I have plans for a completely reworked and more interesting system. While I won't be reworking the maps as a whole this update, I will be adding a full cast of new enemies to the Forest map.

[b]Other Tasks:[/b]I have also added a space for miscellaneous tasks and things that will need to get down before I can fully release the update. This is not a currently exhaustive list and I will be adding to it as development continues and I get a more clear idea of what's missing.

To end off, here's where the roadmap stands after the first week of active development:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44116119/8c3d2cbb711493b6c2c7a193f06e91f18c67a009.png[/img]

Going Forward, I plan to post weekly roadmap updates on my Twitter and Discord, so Follow me there if you wish to see more consistent updates. 

Twitter: https://twitter.com/Elhmok_yt

Discord: https://discord.gg/NdwfnNutqA
